question.text: A particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> moves horizontally between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor which produce an electric field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> in the vertically upward direction. A magnetic induction of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext>2.0</mtext><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> is applied at right angles to the electric field in a direction normal to both <math> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mtext>E</mtext> <mo>→</mo> </mover> </mrow> </math> and <math> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mtext>v</mtext> <mo>→</mo> </mover> </mrow> </math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext>9.8</mtext><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> and the charge on the particle is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>, then the velocity of the charged particle so that it continues to move horizontally is

solution.text:
Net force on the particle should be zero.


            


qE = 1 0 - 6 × 2 0 0 = 2 × 1 0 - 4 N

mg = 2 × 1 0 - 5 × 9.8 = 1.96 × 1 0 - 4 N

Since qE>mg, so magnetic force qvB should act downwards to balance the forces.

qE = mg + qvB ⇒ 2 × 1 0 - 4 = 1.96 × 1 0 - 4 + 1 0 - 6 v × 2

⇒    v = 2 m/s
